bullets: Game 4 of an eight-game single-deck session ('I Got a 96% WIN Rate with this BROKEN Deck'), against a Miner / Wall Breakers bait list with Evo Wall Breakers, Evo Bats, Spear Goblins, Cannon, Bomber and The Log. Win, no crown taken by either side: final towers 2922 / 3870 against 142 / 1076, with Ryley calling it at 666-672s ('that is good game').

The plan is one-lane barrel chip financed by a cheap defence. Goblin Barrel goes out four times (clock 1:57, 1:31, 0:48, 0:31) and only ever right after the opponent has spent — the first one comes off a wasted Log ('Okay, bad log right there. We can go for a goblin barrel now as well', 555-557s). Wall Breakers follow the barrel into the same lane at clock 1:29 to overload the single building.

Lane switch is the win: the right tower is worked down 4164 -> 1634 through double elixir, then from clock 0:48 he moves both barrels to the untouched left tower and takes it 4164 -> 142 in twenty seconds with Ronin and Magic Archer support.

Everything else stays home. Tesla (six placements), Royal Delivery (six), Skeletons (five), Fire Spirit (three) and Ronin (three) are all played on his own half; the only offensive cards are the barrel, Wall Breakers and a Magic Archer that finishes from the bridge at clock 0:25.

He states the deck's cycle condition explicitly at 596-599s — 'Our cycle should be a bit quicker than him as long as we don't use the royal [delivery] too often' — and treats spending Tesla on Wall Breakers as a leak ('I don't want to Tesla the wall breakers too often, but I feel like recently I've been a bit forced to', 601-605s).

Two placement rules he verbalises: Magic Archer goes on the side of his own half 'so they can't activate the king tower off of it' (567-571s), and Wall Breakers get split in the middle on defence 'to take one of the dark prince charges' (636-638s).

The Cannoneer tower troop is named as the enabler — 'having that cannoneer is very nice for us so cuz when we get to the Evo barrel, this guy's just going to be in a complete scramble to defend' (558-563s).

new_deck.display_name: Ronin Goblin Barrel Wall Breakers Bait
new_deck.rationale: Goblin Barrel, Wall Breakers, Skeletons and Fire Spirit all bait the same small spells, and at 2.9 average elixir the deck out-cycles the answers rather than out-muscling them.
new_deck.why_it_works_md: Two 2-3 elixir win conditions in one lane force the defender to hold a building **and** a small spell **and** a swarm at the same time; with a Cannoneer behind him, Ryley can throw a Goblin Barrel and follow it with Wall Breakers a second later and a single Cannon simply cannot cover both — 'The cannon here is going to sell him very hard ... the cannon here is doing absolutely nothing for defense' (587-594s). The defensive half of the deck is deliberately cheap and reactive: Tesla for the ground threats, Royal Delivery for anything that lands on his own half, Skeletons and Fire Spirit as 1-elixir cycle, so the barrel comes back around faster than the answer does — 'Our cycle should be a bit quicker than him as long as we don't use the royal [delivery] too often' (596-599s). Ronin and Magic Archer are the two heavier cards and both are used defensively first, with the Magic Archer converting into a bridge finisher once a tower is low. The failure mode is being forced to spend the building on cheap bait: he calls out Teslaing the opponent's Wall Breakers as something he does not want to do but keeps being pushed into (601-605s).
